get.summary: Stream the health of the cluster
get.description: Answers a server sent events stream that tells, every `every` milliseconds and for as long as the client stays connected, the number of members of the cluster, its health (the worst health of its members: `green` when a member was seen less than half its timeout ago, `orange` under three quarters of it, `red` beyond), and the bytes received from and sent to the workers. Any admin can call it. Only a cluster leader answers it.

parameters.name: every
parameters.description: The interval between two events, in milliseconds: 2000 by default, never less than 1000. A value that is not an integer is ignored

200.description: The stream of the health of the cluster

schema.description: A server sent events stream: every `every` milliseconds, a `data:` line holding as json the number of members (`workers`), the health of the cluster (`health`: `green`, `orange` or `red`), and the bytes received from (`payloadIn`) and sent to (`payloadOut`) the workers, followed by an empty line

put.summary: Apply the quotas updates of a worker
put.description: Applies the quotas updates of the body, one json object per line: the calls of the api keys (`apkincr`), the traffic of the routes (`srvincr`), the counters of the custom quotas (`custquots`) and custom throttling (`custthrot`) plugins, and the statistics of the worker (`globstats`, that also registers the worker as a member). Workers call it on the leaders every `otoroshi.cluster.worker.quotas.pushEvery` milliseconds (2000 by default). The body is gzip compressed when the cluster compression is enabled (`otoroshi.cluster.compression` from 0 to 9), without a `Content-Encoding` header. Every line has to end with a new line, the last one included. A worker identifies itself with the `Otoroshi-Worker-*` headers (its name, id, version, java version, operating system, location, ports and relay routing settings). Only a super admin can call it.

parameters.name: budget
parameters.description: How long the leader may take to apply the updates, in milliseconds (2000 by default): beyond it, a warning is logged. Workers send their `otoroshi.cluster.worker.quotas.timeout`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Name
parameters.description: The name of the worker (`otoroshi.cluster.worker.name`): the leaders register the worker as a member under this name. A body with a known update and no such header is answered with a server error

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Id
parameters.description: The id the worker generated when it started (`node_` followed by a uuid). A temporary `tmpnode_` id is used when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Version
parameters.description: The version of otoroshi the worker runs, `undefined` when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Java-Version
parameters.description: The java virtual machine of the worker, as a json `JavaVersion`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Os
parameters.description: The operating system of the worker, as a json `OS`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Location
parameters.description: The ip address of the worker (`otoroshi.cluster.selfAddress`, or the one it detected when it started), the `location` of the member; `--` when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Http-Port
parameters.description: The exposed http port of the worker

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Https-Port
parameters.description: The exposed https port of the worker

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Internal-Http-Port
parameters.description: The http port the worker listens on

parameters.description: The https port the worker listens on

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Relay-Routing
parameters.description: The relay routing settings of the worker, as a json `RelayRouting`

get.description: Answers the whole state the workers load from the leaders: every key of the datastore (except the audit and alert events, the admins, the backoffice sessions, the health checks and the statistics), one json object per line. A leader answers the copy of the state it refreshes on its own, and registers the caller as a worker member when it sends an `Otoroshi-Worker-Name` header. A worker identifies itself with the `Otoroshi-Worker-*` headers (its name, id, version, java version, operating system, location, ports and relay routing settings). A worker answers its own datastore. The body is gzip compressed when the cluster compression is enabled (`otoroshi.cluster.compression` from 0 to 9), without a `Content-Encoding` header. get.summary: Open the websocket of the state of the cluster
get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket on which the leader pushes the state of the cluster, and the worker sends its quotas updates, instead of polling `GET /api/cluster/state` and `PUT /api/cluster/quotas` (used by the workers when `otoroshi.cluster.worker.useWs` is enabled). Every `otoroshi.cluster.worker.state.pollEvery` milliseconds, the leader sends a json message holding the state (`state`, the bytes of the lines of `GET /api/cluster/state` as an array of numbers), the name and the version of the leader (`node_name`, `node_version`), and the number of lines, the digest and the date of the state (`data_count`, `data_digest`, `data_from`); as a binary message when the cluster compression is enabled, as a text message otherwise. The worker sends text messages holding itself as a member (`member`, a `MemberView`) and an update (`payload`, a `ClusterQuotasUpdate`: only `apkincr`, `srvincr` and `globstats` are applied). Only a super admin can open it.

101.description: The connection is upgraded to a websocket

post.description: Routes, as if this instance had received it, a request another instance of the cluster relays because only this one can reach the backend of its route (relay routing). The relayed request is described by the `Otoroshi-Relay-Routing-*` headers: its id, method, uri, client address, whether it came over https and has a body, its cookies, its client certificates (`Otoroshi-Relay-Routing-Certs-<index>`, PEM encoded) and its headers (`Otoroshi-Relay-Routing-Header-<name>`); the body is the body of the relayed request. The answer is the answer of the route, its headers renamed `Otoroshi-Relay-Routing-Response-Header-<name>`. Only a super admin can call it.
